A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CORRECT and CORRECT-Error. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and substantial additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original error-localization experiments, schema ablations, and human evaluation of synthetic trajectories in Sections 4–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds streaming adaptation, recovery, robustness, cost, and cross-domain evaluations, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The core schema extraction, retrieval-guided diagnosis, and cache-management pipeline remains. Appendix A.13 adds an explicit adaptation that prompts for an error category instead of a step index. Newly documented clustering and preprocessing details do not establish a redesign of the original pipeline.

E1.justification: The original WHO&WHEN and seven CORRECT-Error tasks remain. v2 adds error-category detection on ProgramDev+ChatDev and AG2+GSM8K, AgentErrorBench evaluations including ALFWorld and WebShop, and streaming adaptation and recovery scenarios. These substantially broaden task requirements and evaluated environments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LLM-as-a-Judge, fine-tuning, and naive ICL and adds MIPRO as an evaluated comparator. The new recovery experiment also compares CORRECT-selected restart steps against random restart steps.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate incoming-domain cache fractions, truncation budgets, retrieval noise at fixed k=5, error-category recall, and restart success. Section 4.2 also changes the stated human-labeler count from three to conflicting counts of four and five; the actual revised study size and whether it was rerun remain unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original transfer, cache-size, schema-count, oracle, and self-detection analyses. It adds streaming adaptation, similarity/hotness sensitivity, context-truncation and retrieval-noise tests, targeted recovery, and a multi-error failure case explaining prediction of Step 12 instead of the annotated Step 4.

E5.justification: Section 5 changes the reported aggregate from average performance to median performance over five independent runs. The stated run count remains five; no new confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises several entries, including CORRECT's GPT-5 Human-Crafted Acc@1 from 37.8 to 32.3; aggregation also changes, so this does not establish a same-protocol performance decline. Table 2 remains unchanged. New results include AgentErrorBench scores, streaming and robustness measurements, and restart success of 20% versus 10% for random restarts.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a mathematical specification of silhouette scores and the cluster-count stopping condition S(K+1)-S(K)<epsilon. The decisive-error definition and retrieval equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal claims about training-free schema reuse, the over-2,000-trajectory benchmark, and up-to-19.8% localization improvement remain. v2 removes the abstract's assertion that CORRECT substantially narrows the gap to human-level error recognition, modestly narrowing the claimed impact.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A.11 add substantive limitations concerning ambiguous decisive-error labels, potentially suboptimal semantic retrieval, and later salient errors overshadowing the earliest decisive error. Appendix A.8 discusses feedback dependence and possible automated validation. These considerably expand the explanation of applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents SFT training splits, learning-rate and batch-size searches and selected values, cluster-count selection, encoder context limits, and per-turn truncation. Appendix A.9 supplies error-injection prompts, and the abstract adds a public-code link. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that previously reported experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MIPRO, production-agent motivation, LLaMAFactory, and AgentErrorBench. Appendix A.7 explicitly contrasts CORRECT with static human-curated MAST taxonomies, and A.8 discusses EcoAssistant. The central positioning around training-free schema reuse remains intact.

P1.justification: Introduction and contribution passages are tightened, method explanations gain an algorithm walkthrough, and limitations, impact, and additional appendix headings are introduced. The original main-section progression and much of the existing narrative remain, with most expansion attributable to added scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. Existing plots are regrouped into multipanel Figures 1 and 4–6, and the trajectory-length plot moves to Appendix A.2. Table 1 gains a comparator row, while new result tables and injection-prompt panels substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v1's dynamic-deployment and near-zero-overhead claims had limited direct experimental support. v2 adds streaming, recovery, cost, and retrieval-robustness evaluations, substantially improves implementation documentation, and explains a concrete failure mechanism. These strengthen evidence and reproducibility beyond merely adding benchmark scores. Conflicting human-labeler counts and Table 1's new mislabeling of absolute point differences as relative improvements reduce reporting precision, but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
